payload.reason: The evidence provides a clear description of how crowd workers were instructed to identify important elements in large document collections using a novel crowdsourcing scheme called low-context importance annotation.

claims.text: Crowd workers were instructed to determine important elements in document clusters without reading all documents, using only a description of the topic and propositions.
The crowdsourcing scheme involved collecting Likert-scores from workers for propositions to rank their importance, allowing for efficient and scalable annotation.
The task design was simple and intuitive, enabling workers to quickly assess the importance of propositions based on minimal context.
